Hi Samir / Priya 

Thanks again for the demo today  great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so were aligned on the POC and environment choice.

Call highlights / success criteria (as agreed):
- Achieve sub-500ms median latency on 2k concurrent inference calls for the primary prompt set.
- End-to-end cost per 1k tokens <= our target (we discussed different model/quantization trade-offs).
- Data isolation for customer data during evaluation; logs retained for 30 days and accessible via our Console.
- Functional acceptance tests: generation quality on 3 canonical prompts, embeddings for search, and end-to-end throughput test.

Evaluation plan / roles: 
- Redwood: Marissa (AE) will coordinate timelines and commercial items; Vivek (SE) will own environment setup and test runbooks.
- AcmeAI: Samir will own engineering coordination and provide firewall/IP info; Priya will run quality review and sign off.

Environment options (we discussed during the call):
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted trial with isolated tenant + prefix/KV caching. Minimal networking required.
2) Dedicated sandbox: Reserved GPU pool for ACME with predictable throughput for the POC (more setup time & higher cost).
3) Hosted VPC (recommended middle ground): Redwood-managed control plane + VPC peering (or customer-managed VPC with private endpoints)  gives isolation without on-prem install.

Immediate ask / proposed timeline:
- Please confirm which environment you prefer by EOD Monday 11/30. If youre undecided, we can start with Hosted VPC and move to Dedicated if we need larger throughput.
- Vivek will follow up with a short network checklist (ports, IP allowlist) and a proposed test runbook by Monday.
- Trial target window: start week of Dec 7, core validation completed by Dec 18.

Attachments: Im including our POC checklist and the network requirements spreadsheet for your network/team to review.

Next steps summary:
- Samir: confirm environment preference + share networking contact.
- Priya: confirm success criteria above or add any additional acceptance tests.
- Vivek: deliver network checklist + runbook by 11/30.
- Ill send the trial agreement and a calendar invite for kickoff once environment is selected.

Thanks  looking forward to getting you up and running.

Hi all 

Thanks Marissa  quick technical clarifications from my side to help you decide:

1) Hosted trial:
- Pros: fastest to spin up (same-day), no config changes on your side besides IP allowlist if you want to lock to ACME egress.
- Cons: shared underlying pool; we provide tenant isolation but not a fully reserved GPU.

2) Dedicated sandbox:
- Pros: guaranteed capacity (reserved GPUs), deterministic throughput for stress testing.
- Cons: ~2-3 business days to provision and extra coordination for capacity sizing.

3) Hosted VPC (recommended for POC):
- Options: a) Redwood-managed VPC peering (preferred for speed), b) Customer-managed VPC with Private Link.
- Network notes: for peering we ask for a /28 for our egress if you want to lock down; for Private Link well provide endpoints and a short template for route table entries.

Initial checklist Ill send separately includes:
- IP ranges + CIDR suggestion for allowlisting,
- Firewall ports (TCP 443 primarily, optional 22 for debug with strict controls),
- TLS fingerprinting and cert guidance,
- Test payload sizes for throughput run (we recommend batch sizes and concurrency targets).

If you expect to run heavy throughput tests early, Dedicated may make results cleaner. For most first-pass quality + latency evaluations, Hosted VPC hits the balance between isolation and speed-to-start.

Ill attach a short runbook and the network checklist in a follow-up by EOD.

 Vivek
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
